references.text: The concrete hospitality in Genesis presupposes the theological entry into God's house as described in the psalm.
Clear parallel in the time of the patriarchs: foreign leaders offer space and protection to God's people.
Strong parallel in the theology of hospitality: receiving God's messengers with joy and recognition.
Parallel in the principle of 'space': human hospitality reflects God's ability to receive.
Romans 12:13 encourages the kind of hospitality that Laban practices in Genesis 24:31.
